1. Core Clinical Tension: A 27-year-old male who underwent orthotopic liver transplantation for an infiltrative hepatic cyst presents one year later on immunosuppressive therapy with multiple simultaneous solitary lesions in the brain and lung parenchyma. The primary tension is differentiating between metastatic malignancy / post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder and aggressive parasitic metastatic dissemination spurred by immunosuppressive therapy.
2. Admission Breakpoint: Evaluation at 1-year post-transplant surveillance when brain and chest CT scans reveal multiple nodular parenchymal lesions, prior to invasive tissue biopsies.
3. Differential Distinctions: Metastatic liver cancer or post-transplant de novo malignancy is strongly suspected due to multiorgan parenchymal metastases under immunosuppression, but tissue biopsy proves parasitic recurrence. Pre-existing extrahepatic spread is ruled out by negative pre-transplant whole-body staging. Recurrent alveolar echinococcosis metastasis is confirmed by histopathologic biopsy.
case_prompt: A 27-year-old male presents for clinical evaluation one year after undergoing liver transplantation for an extensive, unresectable infiltrative hepatic lesion. He is maintained on chronic post-transplant immunosuppressive therapy. Pre-transplant whole-body examinations and cross-sectional imaging had confirmed no extrahepatic lesions prior to surgery. Current diagnostic evaluation including brain computed tomography (CT) and thoracic CT demonstrates multiple solitary nodular lesions distributed throughout the brain and lung parenchyma.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Metastatic liver cancer / De novo malignancy
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered as the primary differential diagnosis for new-onset simultaneous multiorgan parenchymal masses in an immunosuppressed transplant recipient, but excluded when histopathological biopsy confirmed parasitic metacestode proliferative tissue rather than malignant neoplasia.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Radical hepatic resection is the most effective treatment for liver cancers.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Pre-existing extrahepatic metastasis prior to transplantation
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered as an explanation for multi-organ involvement, but excluded by comprehensive pre-transplant clinical examination and whole-body imaging confirming no lesions outside the liver.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: No echinococcal lesions were found in the other parts of the body before the transplant surgery.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Follow-up computed tomography of the brain and thorax 1 year post-transplant demonstrated multiple parenchymal lesions, which upon tissue biopsy were confirmed as metastatic alveolar echinococcal recurrences exacerbated by post-transplantation immunosuppressive therapy.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Multiple solitary lesions were observed in the brain and lung parenchyma (Figure 2). The lesions were biopsied and diagnosed as alveolar echinococcal metastasis.

editor_comments: Case prompt strictly terminates at CT imaging before tissue biopsy. Quotes verified verbatim against original case report text.
